title: SK hynix Drives up to 5x Faster Time-to-First-Token with MARS; HBF Expands Capacity by 14x
source_used: TrendForce (on-site summary from the OCP Global Summit 2026)
key_facts: At the OCP Global Summit 2026, Hoshik Kim, senior vice president at SK hynix, introduced MARS (Memory-Centric AI Rack-Scale System), a rack-scale system that pools memory so compute and memory resources are shared.
Kim said that in a multi-turn AI-agent inference service MARS gave a 3 to 5 times improvement in time to first token over recomputation, with tail latency dramatically reduced.
MARS stores the exploding KV cache of multi-turn agents in a shared memory system without exhausting GPU memory and storage.
High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) has about half the bandwidth of HBM but roughly 14 times the capacity, Kim said.
OCP HBF spec version 0.7 was released in July; version 1.0 is expected early next year; a concept prototype is in development; HBF Cube samples are planned for early 2028.
The figures are SK hynix's own; no outside test is reported.
quote_evidence: So if you look at this graph, we have a very good 3 to 5 times improvement in TTFT (Time To First Token) over recomputation, which is quite impressive, especially when you talk about this tail latency, tail latency is dramatically reduced.
HBF is typically half the bandwidth of HBM, but more like 14 times higher capacity than HBM,
and we’ll sample HBF Cube available early 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: Pooled memory aims to make AI agents respond faster without adding more GPUs.
event_date: OCP Global Summit 2026 (exact day of the talk not stated; TrendForce posted 13 Oct 2026)
notes: Company claims from a conference talk, summarised by TrendForce; no independent test. Headline says up to 5x, the quoted figure is 3 to 5 times.
